Relevel in correspondence to another factor

Source: R/simple_relevel.R
simple_relevel.Rd

Function to relevel a variable in accordance to a another variable of class "factor".

Usage

simple_relevel(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
simple_relevel(x, ..., by)

# Default S3 method
simple_relevel(x, by, map, value = c("unsorted", "sorted", "levels"), ...)

Arguments

x

For the data.frame method: a data.frame (passing it as `data = ` is deprecated). For the default method: a vector that will be relevelled.

...

For the data.frame method: unquoted variable names that will be relevelled. Unused by the default method.

by

For the data.frame method: an unquoted variable name the relevelling process will base on. For the default method: a vector that the relevelling process will base on.

map

a list that links by to x in the form of list(by.1 = c(x1.1, x1.2...), by.2 = c(x2.1, x2.2...)) or a data.frame with two columns "from" and "to" serving the same purpose.

value

a string: whether to return

- "levels": new levels only

- "unsorted" (default): an unsorted, relevelled factor

- "sorted": a sorted, relevelled factor

Value

An object of the same class as the input

A factor or a numeric vector of order

Examples

df <- data.frame(g = factor(c("b", "a", "b", "a"), levels = c("b", "a")),
                 x = c("x1", "y1", "x2", "y2"))
levels(simple_relevel(df, x, by = g)$x)
#> [1] "x1" "x2" "y1" "y2"
simple_relevel(c("p", "q", "r"), by = factor(c("B", "A", "B"), levels = c("B", "A")),
               map = list(A = "q", B = c("p", "r")), value = "levels")
#> [1] "p" "r" "q"
